# Fire Tools

> Fire Tools is a free, open-source, local-first planner for financial independence (FIRE): FIRE calculator, Monte Carlo and withdrawal-rate simulations, asset allocation, cashflow (expenses and income) and net worth tracking. The desktop app keeps data in a local SQLite database and serves a REST API on loopback that AI agents can use, after the user turns on Settings > Agent access, to onboard someone or log a month. API writes appear in the running app within seconds.

Agents should install the `using-fire-tools` skill below and call the API only through its helper script, which reads the per-launch token from the app's discovery file without printing it. Ask the user before writing, never request or reveal the token, and do not use the public demo for real data: it is read-only.

## Agents

- [Agent skill: using-fire-tools](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/agents/using-fire-tools/SKILL.md): onboarding and monthly logging workflow, ground rules, errors
- [Agent API reference](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/agents/using-fire-tools/references/api.md): discovery file, state endpoints, changesets, worked onboarding example
- [Data model](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/agents/using-fire-tools/references/data-model.md): enums, expense categories with Need/Want defaults, field rules
- [Helper script](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/agents/using-fire-tools/scripts/fire-tools-api.mjs): Node.js 18+ client that adds the token and refuses non-local targets

## Docs

- [Use Fire Tools with an AI agent](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/docs/user/ai-agents.html): how a user enables agent access and installs the skill

- [OpenAPI contract](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/api/openapi.yaml): every route, request and response
- [User guide](https://fire-tools-inc.github.io/app/docs/user/): what each tool does
